subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope and measurement environment should define the native-Linux VPS performance runbook for this issue?
rationale: The request is valid but broad, and automation cannot safely choose the VPS profile, latency budget, required measurements, or boundary between documentation, instrumentation, and code optimization.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Define the native-Linux host profile, required telemetry, and acceptance criteria before queueing focused instrumentation or optimization work.

options.title: Split to narrower instrumentation issues
options.body: Convert the broad request into separate context, memory, compaction, Telegram, and gateway diagnostics issues that can land independently.

options.title: Treat as support-only
options.body: Close or defer the broad analysis and point users to existing OTEL, VPS, memory, and Telegram docs until a concrete reproducible bottleneck is supplied.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Define the native-Linux host profile, required telemetry, and acceptance criteria before queueing focused instrumentation or optimization work.

likelyOwner.reason: The accessible history points most strongly to this contributor across the current gateway/docs/context surfaces needed to set scope.
